title: Understanding Rapid Test Kit Technology
desc: How a rapid drug test is built, how it produces a result, the device formats and specimen types you will handle, the rules that govern their use, and the limits every collector must understand before reading a single result.

title: Drug Classes and Emerging Substances
desc: A reference to every major drug class: stimulants, opioids, sedatives, cannabinoids, hallucinogens, and others. Covers what each drug turns into in the body, which tests detect it, which prescriptions explain it, and the new substances that standard panels miss.

title: Rapid Test Kit Types and Specimens
desc: The rapid test formats available for urine, oral fluid, and hair, the strengths and trade-offs of each, how long each specimen can detect use, and the collection practices that keep donors from defeating the test.

title: Specimen Collections and Procedures
part: PART II COLLECTION AND LABORATORY TESTING
desc: Regulated and non-regulated collections, the custody forms that go with them, and best practices for laboratory-based urine, oral fluid, hair, breath alcohol, and fingernail collections.

title: Understanding Laboratory Testing
part: PART II COLLECTION AND LABORATORY TESTING
desc: What happens to a specimen after it leaves your clinic: the two-step screen and confirmation process, the instruments behind each step, how specimens are accessioned and tracked, why some results take longer, and how cut-offs, split specimens, and retained specimens work.

title: Reading Package Inserts and Resolving Discrepancies
part: PART II COLLECTION AND LABORATORY TESTING
desc: How to read a package insert, why a negative is not zero, how class assays and cross-reactivity explain most "failed" results, and a step-by-step method, with a worksheet, for deciding whether a rapid test performed as expected.

title: Understanding the MRO Process
part: PART III REVIEW AND SPECIALIZED TESTING
desc: Who the Medical Review Officer is, what happens between a laboratory result and a final result, every outcome an MRO can report, how donors interact with the MRO, how a laboratory positive can become a verified negative, and how the MRO protects clinics, donors, and employers.

title: Alcohol Testing and Biomarkers
part: PART III REVIEW AND SPECIALIZED TESTING
desc: How alcohol moves through the body, the tests that measure it now (breath, saliva, blood) and the biomarkers that show drinking hours, days, weeks, or months ago (EtG, EtS, PEth, and hair EtG), how to choose between them, and how to handle incidental exposure.

title: Communicating Results
desc: The right words for every result, what collectors can and cannot say to donors, how to report to clients without overstating a screen, how to handle pressure, and difficult conversations, and how to document every communication.

title: Privacy and Confidentiality
desc: Which laws protect drug testing information, who may receive a result, how to get valid authorization, how to protect privacy at the front desk and in records, how to handle subpoenas, and what to do when information goes to the wrong place.

title: Quality Control and Compliance
desc: How a clinic proves its testing is reliable: the CLIA Certificate of Waiver, external quality control, lot verification, storage monitoring, staff competency, written procedures, corrective action, and the records an inspector will ask to see. Includes ready-to-use logs and a self-audit checklist.
